summary: The call with an offer: {the offerer} offers {the job}, and the player must say yes or no before the household's bills come due.
realLife: One life: A twenty-five-year-old near St. Louis who missed a call from a security company's hiring office, returned it, interviewed and was hired as a receptionist at fourteen dollars an hour. The hours let her and her boyfriend share the one car. She still faced a backlog of bills that delayed their plans. Another: A fifty-year-old with a master's degree who had earned over six figures until his employer collapsed in 2002. After more than a year out and hundreds of applications he took a ten-dollar-an-hour work-from-home job, where take-home would be below his unemployment check. He weighed pride against ending the joblessness. Another: He was laid off again, then took an offer at about a third of his old pay with benefits, and was dismissed less than a week into training after failing an exam. A woman laid off from IT weighed selling her ring or house, then took a lower-paid job at a law firm. Another: After nearly five years in prison on drug charges he took whatever work he could find. Housemates in his sober living home invited him to volunteer at a food bank, and in 2021 its director interviewed him and gave him a warehouse job because she believed in him.
